name: Ireland
snapshot: A rich, fast-growing country dependent on US tech and pharma giants, where a housing crisis dominates politics and a left-wing independent won the presidency in 2025.
culture: Ireland's literary tradition, from Joyce and Yeats to Sally Rooney, and its music, from trad sessions to U2, punch far above its size. Gaelic games, hurling and Gaelic football, draw huge crowds. Irish is the first official language, and Gaeltacht areas keep it alive. St Patrick's Day is celebrated worldwide by a vast diaspora.
society: Ireland went from one of Western Europe's poorest countries to one of its richest, thanks largely to US multinationals drawn by low corporate tax; Apple, Google and Pfizer have European hubs there. Housing shortages and homelessness are acute. Voters legalised same-sex marriage and abortion in landmark referendums in 2015 and 2018.
situation: Micheál Martin of Fianna Fáil became Taoiseach again in January 2025 in a coalition with Fine Gael and independents. Catherine Connolly, a left-wing independent, won the presidential election in October 2025 by a landslide. Ireland holds the rotating presidency of the Council of the EU in the second half of 2026, while its economy, built on US multinationals, watches Washington's tariff threats against pharmaceuticals closely.
power: A parliamentary republic. The Taoiseach leads the majority in the Dáil, elected by single transferable vote; the directly elected president is largely ceremonial.

eat: Irish stew of lamb and potato
argue: Relying on US tech giants and their taxes

say.name: Irish (English is spoken by nearly everyone)

story: England began conquering Ireland in the 12th century. The Great Famine of the 1840s killed a million and drove another million to emigrate. After the Easter Rising and a war of independence, the Irish Free State was created in 1922, leaving Northern Ireland in the UK. The Troubles in the north killed 3,500 until the Good Friday Agreement in 1998. The 'Celtic Tiger' economy boomed.
